blogs.title: The Safe Scan: Leveraging Non-Contrast MRI for Diagnosing Abdominal Masses in Pregnancy
blogs.description: This post delves into the diagnostic dilemma of differentiating uterine leiomyomas from adnexal masses using safe imaging modalities. It highlights why non-contrast MRI is the gold standard over ultrasound alone for mapping mass anatomy and clarifies the safety guidelines regarding gadolinium use during pregnancy.

blogs.title: CA-125 in Pregnancy: A Diagnostic Trap for Non-Gynecologic Clinicians
blogs.description: A deep dive into the physiological fluctuations of CA-125 during gestation. This blog explains why a single elevated value can mimic malignancy in older patients, emphasizing the necessity of longitudinal trends and the specific median ranges for the second trimester to avoid unnecessary interventions.

blogs.title: The Symptom Threshold: When to Operate on Symptomatic Uterine Leiomyomas
blogs.description: This piece analyzes the decision-making matrix for surgical intervention in pregnancy. It explores the tension between expectant management and risk of torsion, necrosis, or rupture, using the case of a twisted pedicle myoma to define clear indications for laparotomy or myomectomy.

blogs.title: Obstetric Roadblocks: How Posterior Intramural Myomas Dictate Delivery Mode
blogs.description: Focusing on the 'hard obstetric' outcomes, this post discusses how the anatomical location of large uterine masses impacts the physical delivery phase. It reviews evidence on why posterior or obstructive lesions often necessitate elective Cesarean sections to prevent uterine rupture or mechanical obstruction.

blogs.title: Compressing the Diaphragm: Distinguishing Pregnancy-Related Dyspnea from Mass Effect
blogs.description: This blog tackles the differential diagnosis for dyspnea in a pregnant patient with massive abdominal pathology. It differentiates between pulmonary causes (like PE) and mechanical compression from tumors, explaining how mass size and location can mimic cardiac or respiratory insufficiencies.
